title: Finance Manager Salary Melbourne: Hourly to Annual Conversion Guide
description: Convert a finance manager salary Melbourne hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, super, and award rate comparisons using official data.
salarySummary: Based on the ABS average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, a finance manager salary in Melbourne equates to approximately $108,352 per year (assuming 38 hours per week).

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $50 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements. On this site, you enter your base hourly rate and then check the casual loading box to add 25%. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading. For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your salary at 12% of your ordinary earnings (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your pay. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. For a salary of $100,000, super would be an additional $12,000 per year, bringing total employer cost to $112,000.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion from Hourly to Annual Pay

When you’re evaluating a job offer or negotiating a salary, converting an hourly rate to an annual figure is a straightforward but essential calculation. The standard formula is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**

For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, which is the ordinary hours under most awards and the National Employment Standards. This gives you a consistent annual figure to compare against salaried roles. The same formula works for part-time or casual work – just use your actual weekly hours.

Many employers pay fortnightly, so you can also calculate your fortnightly gross pay by multiplying your weekly pay by two. For example, if your weekly pay is $1,000, your fortnightly pay is $2,000 before tax and other deductions.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage increased to $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award minimum wages rose by 4.75% on the same date. Casual employees covered by an award receive a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate, bringing the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour.

These rates are the legal floor. Many professional roles, including finance managers, are paid well above award rates and may be covered by enterprise agreements or be award-free. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help you check the correct award for your industry.

## Finance Manager Salary Melbourne: What the Data Shows

When researching a **finance manager salary Melbourne**, official data provides a useful benchmark. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in May 2026 averaged $2,083.70 per week. Annualising that figure:

$2,083.70 × 52 = $108,352.40 per year

This is the average across all full-time occupations, not just finance managers. Specific finance manager roles in Melbourne often command higher salaries, particularly in financial services, corporate headquarters, or large consulting firms. However, without a dedicated ABS survey for that occupation, we rely on this broad measure as a starting point.

To find the hourly equivalent of that average: $2,083.70 ÷ 38 hours = $54.83 per hour. So if you’re offered an hourly rate for a finance manager role in Melbourne, you can compare it against this figure to see if it aligns with market norms.

## Fortnightly Pay and Tax Considerations

Most Australian employees are paid fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the ABS average: $2,083.70 × 2 = $4,167.40 per fortnight.

Tax is withheld by your employer using the PAYG system. For the 2026–27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Most residents also pay the Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The Australian Taxation Office provides tax tables and a withheld calculator to check your take-home pay.

For a finance manager earning $108,352 per year, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $26,000–$28,000, depending on deductions and offsets. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual salary is $108,352, your employer must contribute an additional $13,002.24 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay – it’s an extra cost to the employer.

When comparing a salary offer, always consider the total employment cost, including super. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Important Distinctions

It’s crucial to understand the differences between:

- **National Minimum Wage**: The legal minimum for award-free employees ($26.44 per hour).
- **Award rates**: Minimum pay rates set by industry awards, often higher than the national minimum.
- **Casual loading**: An extra 25% on the base rate for casual employees, compensating for lack of paid leave.
- **Superannuation**: Paid on top of your salary, not included in the hourly or annual rate.

On this site, the calculator assumes you enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, check the casual loading box to add 25% – do not enter a rate that already includes the loading. The annual figure shown is your gross pay before tax and super.

For a full list of award pay guides, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. To explore average earnings across industries, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay).

## Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
